reader_question: Where do Federal Reserve officials expect unemployment to go, and how wide is the range?
grade_line: Documented: the Federal Reserve’s Summary of Economic Projections, September 16, 2026, and the Bureau of Labor Statistics’ unemployment rate
title: Federal Reserve officials projected a median unemployment rate of 4.1 percent for each year through 2029, and past forecast errors put 2029’s range at 2.0 to 6.2 percent.
measure_line: Unemployment rate, average for the fourth quarter of each year, United States: actual for 2021 to 2024, the four years before the projections with a full fourth quarter, and projected in September 2026 for 2026 to 2029 and the longer run. The outer band spans the median plus and minus the average error of past forecasts, a range the Board says holds the outcome with about a 70 percent probability.
reading_guide: The thin line at the left is where the rate stood. The thick line is the officials’ median; the narrow inner band spans every official’s projection, and the wide outer band shows how far past forecasts have missed.
notes: Method: the line is the median of officials’ projections, each under that official’s view of appropriate policy; the outer band adds and subtracts the average error of past forecasts, 2006 to 2025, which the Board says covers about 70 percent of outcomes under certain assumptions. The longer run has no error band.
The officials are the members of the Board of Governors and the presidents of the 12 Reserve Banks.
The actual fourth-quarter averages were 4.2 percent in 2021, 3.6 in 2022, 3.8 in 2023 and 4.1 in 2024. The year 2025 has none, since no unemployment rate was published for October 2025.
alt: A fan chart of the unemployment rate projected for 2026 to 2029. The median holds at 4.1 percent each year, inside a narrow band for the range of all officials’ projections and a wide band from past forecast errors that grows to 2.0 to 6.2 percent by 2029. The longer run sits apart at 4.2 percent. At the left, a thinner line shows the actual rate’s fourth-quarter average: 4.2 percent in 2021, 3.6 in 2022, 3.8 in 2023 and 4.1 in 2024, with no figure for 2025.

table.caption: Projections of the unemployment rate, fourth quarter of each year, percent

chart_notes: The thin line at the left is the actual rate, and the light column at 2025 marks the year with no fourth-quarter average. The wide outer band is the median plus and minus past forecast errors; the narrow inner band is the range of all officials’ projections. Thin gray lines edge both bands. The longer run is drawn apart, at the right, with its range as a line.
